name: Question 12
problem:
Consider the following statement. 

If $f(x)=4{x}^{2}-x+5,$ then $f=O(1)$ as $x\to 0.$

A proof of the statement is given below.

$\text{L1}:\,f=O(4{x}^{2}-x+5)$

$\text{L2}:\,{lim}_{x\to 0}(\frac{4{x}^{2}-x}{5})=0$  

$\text{L3}:\,4{x}^{2}-x=O(5)$  as $x\to 0$ 

$\text{L4}:\,f=O(5)$  as $x\to 0$   

$\text{L5}:\,f=O(1)$  as $x\to 0$ 

Select the correct options to justify each step of the reasoning.

$\,$ Line $\text{L1}$ follows from  
{{field-1}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L4}$ follows from lines
